title: The Last Semester
premise: Marguerite Nakamura transfers to Hollow Creek High for her senior year, determined to stay invisible until graduation. But when she's paired with her nemesis, popular girl Delia Voss, for a semester-long local history project, they uncover evidence that the school was built over a demolished neighborhood whose residents were cheated out of their homes decades ago—and that Delia's family profited from it. As their investigation makes them targets and pulls in a found family of misfits, Marguerite must choose between safe anonymity and public truth-telling; the book ends at graduation, where she delivers the project as a public reckoning that forces the town to acknowledge the erased community of Bellhaven Row.
about_author: J. M. Lockridge is a former high school debate coach who grew up in a rust-belt town where half the main street vanished into a parking structure. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to accept the histories adults hand them.

chapters.title: Head Down
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She arrives at Hollow Creek High with strict rules for invisibility: no clubs, no questions, no friends. A tour reveals odd details—the gym sits lower than the rest of the school, and old bricks peek through new tile. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness, the cost of always watching your back.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester-long 'Local Legacies' projects and pairs her with Delia Voss, who humiliated her during orientation week. Their first meeting is pure friction—Delia wants an easy topic; Marguerite wants a good grade and silence. Beat: resentment sharpened by reluctant proximity.

chapters.title: Basement Bricks
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Forced to find a topic, they follow a maintenance door to a sub-basement where foundations don't match any blueprint: a street-level doorway bricked over, house numbers still visible. Delia recognizes her grandmother's maiden name on a plaque. Beat: unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Bellhaven Row
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Library archives reveal Bellhaven Row, a working-class neighborhood condemned in 1971; residents were paid pennies and scattered. The school was built on it within two years. Marguerite feels an unexpected kinship—her own family lost their home once. Beat: the past stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia wants to drop the topic—it touches her family—but can't explain why without confessing. She proposes a truce: finish fast, keep it shallow. Marguerite agrees but secretly photographs everything. Beat: uneasy alliance built on mutual concealment.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Their research attracts Theo (archivist kid), Priya (print journalist hopeful), and Marcus (Delia's ex-best friend), forming a lunch-table alliance. For the first time, Marguerite laughs in a cafeteria. Beat: found family begins assembling around shared purpose.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia finds her late grandmother's locked box: deeds, eviction notices, and letters proving the Voss family bought Bellhaven properties at rigged auction prices. Guilt wars with loyalty. Beat: inheritance revealed as burden.

chapters.title: Someone's Watching
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Copies of their notes go missing; a warning note appears in Marguerite's locker—'some things stay buried.' Principal Reyes confiscates their archive requests. Someone powerful wants this quiet. Beat: fear arrives, stakes become real.

chapters.title: Marcus Splits
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Pressure mounts when Marcus's scholarship situation is quietly threatened after he speaks to a reporter. He quits the group, accusing them of playing hero with other people's lives. Beat: first fracture in the found family; doubt spreads.

chapters.title: The Eviction File
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Theo locates a sealed 1972 settlement: the district knew homes were undervalued and buried the findings. Marguerite realizes staying invisible now means complicity. Beat: her old survival strategy turns against her conscience.

chapters.title: Delia's Confession
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Cornered by Marguerite's questions, Delia admits her family's role and her grandmother's deathbed wish that someone tell the truth. She chooses the project over her family's reputation. Beat: vulnerability as turning point; nemesis becomes ally.

chapters.title: Reyes's Office
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Principal Reyes reveals she's a Bellhaven descendant being pressured by the school board; she warns them the board will expel 'troublemakers' before graduation. She slips them one key document anyway. Beat: adult ally at personal risk; clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Finding Marcus
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. They track down Marcus working nights; instead of apologizing, they offer him authorship of the financial chapter—his name, his risk, his terms. He returns. Beat: repair through respect, not sentiment.

chapters.title: Descendants
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Priya finds living Bellhaven families, including Alma Ruiz, 84, evicted at nineteen. Hearing Alma describe her front porch—the exact spot of the gym—makes the project human. Beat: grief and responsibility deepen; the group commits fully.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The board deletes archive access, and a fire alarm destroys their printed drafts the night before the presentation deadline. Suspicion falls on a board member's son at school. Beat: rage crystallizes into resolve rather than despair.

chapters.title: Backup Everything
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The group rebuilds from cloud copies, Theo's memory, and Alma's testimony recorded on Priya's phone. Working all night in the sub-basement itself, they seal the finished project. Beat: solidarity forged under pressure; the team becomes family.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia's father offers her anything—college money, a car—to bury the project, framing it as protecting her future. She refuses, and he threatens to disown her. Beat: the price of justice made personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Locked Out
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On presentation day, the board cancels the showcase entirely. Reyes is suspended. The group faces a choice: submit quietly and lose, or go public. Marguerite, once the girl who hid, proposes the plan. Beat: inversion of her arc—invisibility abandoned.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. They plan to present during the graduation ceremony's student address slot, which Marguerite earned with top grades. Alma agrees to attend publicly. Fear, nausea, and fierce certainty mingle the night before. Beat: calm before the storm; everyone all-in.

chapters.title: The Last Semester
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At graduation, Marguerite abandons her approved speech and presents Bellhaven Row: documents projected behind her, Alma standing beside her, Delia naming her own family's debt. The auditorium erupts; board members walk out as cameras roll. Beat: climax—truth spoken at maximum cost and maximum witness.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Fallout lands unevenly: a formal inquiry opens, Reyes is reinstated, Delia's father goes silent, and some classmates resent them. But Alma holds Marguerite's hand on the old porch line, and the misfit table stays full. Beat: bittersweet cost-and-gain accounting.

chapters.title: Who to Be
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Summer's first morning: Marguerite packs for college, leaving behind a plaque she and Delia placed at the bricked-over doorway—BELLHAVEN ROW REMEMBERS. She writes to Alma, texts the group chat, and walks out head up. Beat: resolution—belonging chosen, identity claimed, story closed.
